q: E[X] is a value that X can take.
why: For a die, E[X] = 3.5, which you can never roll. The expected value is a long-run average.
Expected values add even when X and Y depend on each other.
True when X and Y are uncorrelated, for example independent. Otherwise add 2·Cov(X, Y).
Constants come out squared: Var(3X) = 3² · 4 = 36. The SD triples, and variance is SD².

q: For independent X and Y, Var(X − Y) = Var(X) − Var(Y).
why: Myth. Variances add: Var(X − Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y). Subtracting a random amount adds uncertainty too.
